mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (غرقا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise (نشطا), (سبحا) and (سبقا).
His saying (أمرا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (المدبرات). It is also said that it is a maṣdar; and also said that it is accusative by dropping the preposition, i.e. "by a command" (بأمر). Its being accusative by (المدبرات) is far-fetched only because the arranging (tadbīr) does not belong to the angels; it belongs only to Allah, exalted be His mention. They are sent with what Allah arranges and wills, and the arranging is not theirs, unless you construe it in the sense that they arrange it by Allah's command to them. The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "By the Lord of these things mentioned, you will surely be resurrected"; what indicates this is their denial of the resurrection in His saying (يقولون أئنا لمردودون في الحافرة). It is also said that the answer is (إن في ذلك لعبرة). It is also said that its answer is (يوم ترجف), with the lām omitted, i.e. "surely on the day it quakes" (ليوم ترجف).

mekki-muskil:16-17.t: His saying (طوى اذهب): (طوى) is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from (الوادي). Whoever reads the ṭāʾ with kasra, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, has it in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like (ثنى), (عدى) and (سوى), its implied form being "in the sacred valley twice". Whoever does not decline it makes it deflected (maʿdūl) from (طاو), like ʿUmar and Zufar, and it is definite. Whoever declines it makes it like (حطم), not deflected. It is also said that it is a diptote only because it is the name of a spot of land and is definite.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (نكال الآخرة): a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (والأرض بعد ذلك): (الأرض) is accusative by an implied verb which (دحاها) explains. The nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject). According to the Basrans the accusative is the preferred choice; al-Farrāʾ said that the nominative and the accusative are equal in it. Its like is (والجبال أرساها).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying (متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying (فأما من طغى): (من) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فإن الجحيم) and what follows it. Its like is (وأما من خاف); but in the khabar a returning pronoun is omitted by which the khabar is completed; its implied form is "the Blaze is the refuge for him" and "the Garden is the refuge for him". It is also said that its implied form is "it is his refuge", and the alif and lām are a compensation for the omitted [pronoun].

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying (أيان مرساها): (مرساها) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أيان) is the khabar (predicate). It is an indeclinable (mabnī) adverbial meaning (متى) "when". It was made indeclinable only because it contains the meaning of the interrogative, which belongs to the particle; since it stood in the place of the particle and was used to ask a question, it was made indeclinable as the particle is; and it was made indeclinable on a vowel because the letter before the last is vowelless.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying (فيم أنت): the alif of (ما) was dropped as it was dropped from (عم) and the like; it is like it in reason and ruling, and it has already been mentioned.
